purpose: Declared tolerances for the cross-platform portability comparison of case outputs. This is NOT a scientific acceptance criterion and is never used for canonical reproduction, which is byte identity checked with diff. It answers one question: running the same case implementation on a different operating system, C library and CPU, did the published scientific result survive?
not_a_threshold: No reservoir-engineering acceptance criterion is expressed here, and none was altered to accommodate these numbers. Each case evaluates its own criteria independently on every environment, and those criterion states are compared EXACTLY, not within a tolerance.

measured_basis.method: A1, A3 and A4 were run from scratch on every environment below and compared leaf by leaf against the canonical container. The tolerance was then chosen from the measured spread, not chosen first and justified afterwards. B1 and B2 were measured after the envelope existed and are recorded here as evidence that it still holds, never as a reason to widen it.
environments: canonical container python:3.13.2-bookworm (Debian 12, glibc 2.36, x86_64) - the reference
ubuntu-24.04 runner, CPython 3.11 - byte-identical to canonical
ubuntu-24.04 runner, CPython 3.12 - byte-identical to canonical
ubuntu-24.04 runner, CPython 3.13.15 (glibc 2.39) - byte-identical to canonical
macos-15 runner, arm64, CPython 3.13 - the only environment that diverges
measured_basis.cause: Ordinary rounding differences between platform libm implementations. Twenty-four transcendental functions were measured to differ by 1 to 4 units in the last place between macOS arm64 and Linux x86_64; math.fsum, math.log, math.sqrt, math.hypot and the Mersenne Twister integer stream are bit-identical, which rules out summation order, seeding and draw order. random.gauss diverges only because it is composed of cos, sin and log.

case_B2_wellbore_storage_window.measured: 2026-09-17, CI run 35146429726, against the committed snapshot
environments_agreeing_exactly: canonical container python:3.13.2-bookworm - byte-identical, checked with diff
macos-15 arm64 CPython 3.13 - every field equal
case_B2_wellbore_storage_window.why_it_is_exact_where_other_cases_are_no: B2's forward model is evaluated by mpmath, which computes in pure Python at 30 decimal digits. Every modified Bessel function and the whole inverse Laplace transform are therefore free of the platform libm differences that put A4 at 2.37e-08 and B1 at 1.11e-10, and the float64 tail -- the Bourdet chain and the least-squares fit -- uses only IEEE-754 operations that are exact and identically ordered on every platform. This is a property of the arithmetic, not a stronger claim about the science.
case_B2_wellbore_storage_window.envelope_consequence: None. B2 needs no tolerance at all: the difference is zero rather than small. The existing 1e-07 envelope is reused unchanged and was not widened, and this case cannot be cited as evidence that the envelope is adequate for cases that do use libm.
case_B2_wellbore_storage_window.caveat: The snapshot was authored on macOS arm64, so the local same-platform comparison is determinism and not portability. The four environments above are what measure portability, and they are the numbers quoted.

default_float.why: Chosen against four measured bounds rather than to make a particular run pass. It sits 4.2x above the worst difference actually observed (2.37e-08), so genuine platform noise passes. It sits 5x below the precision at which this site displays anything (six significant figures, so a rendered value is sensitive at about 5e-07). It sits 2e4 below the margin by which A3's own best-option ranking is decided (best_option_margin_relative = 2.00e-03), so no ordering can reverse inside it. And it sits about 8.6e6 below the tightest acceptance-criterion margin measured (0.864), so no criterion can change state inside it. A failure requires BOTH the relative and the absolute tolerance to be exceeded, so a difference below 1e-12 in absolute terms never fails on its own.

zero_valued_fields.scale_note: reservoir pressures of 1e3 to 1e4 psia, so this floor is about 1e-10 of the working scale
zero_valued_fields.why: A solver convergence residual. Its exact value is zero, so a relative difference divides by the noise being measured: the observed values are around 3e-09 psia and two environments disagreeing there produced an apparent 21 percent relative difference that means nothing.

zero_valued_fields.scale_note: a dimensionless error against an exact analytic oracle; the observed values are at most 3e-13
zero_valued_fields.why: Error against an exact oracle, so the exact value is zero. One environment produced 1.11e-16 where another produced 0.0, which is a relative difference of exactly 1.0 and carries no information.

exact_float_fields.why: a seed is an identifier, not a computed quantity
an acceptance threshold is configuration; if it moves, the criterion moved

platform_dependent_digests.why: A SHA-256 taken over the case's own floating-point payload. It is an integrity device for the canonical environment, where it is compared byte for byte along with every other byte and no tolerance applies. Across platforms it can only report that something differs, because a single one-ULP difference anywhere in the payload changes every bit of the hash. That question is already answered, leaf by leaf and with the magnitude attached, by this comparison itself, which is strictly stronger than the digest: excluding the digest removes no detection power, whereas comparing it exactly would fail every case that touches a divergent libm function for a reason that has nothing to do with the reservoir engineering.
platform_dependent_digests.detection_is_not_lost_because: B1 carries 1100 float leaves, all of which are compared individually against the declared envelope. A corrupted payload changes at least one of them and is caught there. A payload the digest would flag but the leaf comparison would not does not exist, because the digest is computed from those same leaves.
platform_dependent_digests.still_reported: The comparator counts digest fields and prints the differing reference and candidate values, so an excluded digest is visible in the report rather than silently dropped.
platform_dependent_digests.measured_when_added: Introduced for case B1. On ubuntu-24.04 CPython 3.13 against the macOS-produced reference, B1 showed 1100 float fields with a worst relative difference of 1.113506e-10 and a worst absolute difference of 1.776357e-15 -- three orders of magnitude inside the 1e-07 envelope -- while metrics_sha256 differed completely. That contrast is the whole argument for this rule.
